agent_answer:
Raj was describing the tension between paid commercial work and his personal creative work: he feels commercial contracts eat up the hours meant for his own projects, and he keeps taking them (he has another big one starting next month). Even though the current food contract is "technically good money," he calls it "spiritually corrosive," and he says that after it ends he wants a month with no client language near him and intends to work on personal projects only.

Luca already knew it: Luca preemptively advised Raj to let the commercial work pay for the quiet months "without letting it get to define the work," which directly addresses Raj's recurring conflict. Luca's closing line — "the work will be ready when it's ready for all of us. Raj, you know where I am" — also shows familiarity with Raj's cycle of feeling drained by client work and needing a route back to his own creative space.
